root_cause: No min-instances configured on staging; scale-from-zero cold start (~80-90s, inherited from live production's own startup-time corpus loading) exceeded typical external prober timeouts.
fix: Set --min-instances=1 on staging only via async deploy + bounded polling.
known_limitations: A transient cold-start window (up to ~90s) still occurs immediately after any staging redeploy while Cloud Run cycles the rollout instance for a steady-state min-instance one; this is expected and bounded, not an unbounded hang.
Production (pathology-hub-v04) was not modified, inspected for this fix beyond a read-only traffic re-check, or given min-instances -- out of scope for this session.

No application code was changed to fix this; a lazy-loading refactor of the recovered baseline's startup handlers was considered but deliberately not attempted (see docs/STAGING_HEALTH_DEBUG_V0_2_20260705.md for reasoning).
